L7: ## Abstract
L8: This paper presents the key algorithmic techniques behind CatBoost, a new gradient boosting toolkit. Their combination leads to CatBoost outperforming other publicly available boosting implementations in terms of quality on a variety of datasets. Two critical algorithmic advances introduced in CatBoost are the implementation of ordered boosting, a permutation-driven alternative to the classic algorithm, and an innovative algorithm for processing categorical features.
L9: Both techniques were created to fight a prediction shift caused by a special kind of target leakage present in all currently existing implementations of gradient boosting algorithms. In this paper, we provide a detailed analysis of this problem and demonstrate that proposed algorithms solve it effectively, leading to excellent empirical results.

L225: # TabPFN
L226: 
L227: ## Quick Start
L228: 
L229: ### Interactive Notebook Tutorial
L230: 
L231: Tip
L232: 
L233: Dive right in with our interactive Colab notebook! It's the best way to get a hands-on feel for TabPFN, walking you through installation, classification, and regression examples.
L234: ### Installation
L235: 
L236:     pip install tabpfn
L237: 
L238: TabPFN supports Python 3.10+.
L239: 
L240: > ⚡ GPU Recommended: For optimal performance, use a GPU (even older ones with ~8GB VRAM work well; 16GB needed for some large datasets). On CPU, only moderate datasets are feasible (TabPFN-3, TabPFN-3.5 and TabPFN-3.5-Fast allow up to 5000 samples; older versions up to 1000). No GPU? Use our free hosted inference via 【106†TabPFN Client】.
L241: On macOS: GPU support is automatically included for Apple Silicon Macs. For best performance, ensure you are using PyTorch 2.13 or newer (see 【107†#949】).
L242: 
L243: On Linux: Nvidia GPU support is automatically included. For AMD GPUs, first 【108†install PyTorch with ROCm†pytorch.org】, then install TabPFN. For example,
L244: 
L245:     pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.2
L246:     pip install tabpfn
L247: For a CPU-only install, first 【108†install CPU-only PyTorch†pytorch.org】, then install TabPFN. This saves disk space if you do not have a GPU.
L248: 
L249: On Windows: For Nvidia GPUs, 【108†install PyTorch with CUDA†pytorch.org】, then install TabPFN. For AMD GPUs, 【109†install PyTorch with ROCm†rocm.docs.amd.com】, then install TabPFN.
L250: ### Basic Usage
L251: 
L252: To use our default TabPFN-3.5 model:
L253: 
L254:     from tabpfn import TabPFNClassifier, TabPFNRegressor
L255: 
L256:     clf = TabPFNClassifier()
L257:     clf.fit(X_train, y_train)  # downloads checkpoint on first use
L258:     predictions = clf.predict(X_test)
L259: 
L260:     reg = TabPFNRegressor()
L261:     reg.fit(X_train, y_train)  # downloads checkpoint on first use
L262:     predictions = reg.predict(X_test)
L263: To use the smaller, faster TabPFN-3.5-Fast you can use `ModelVersion.V3_5_FAST` or "v3.5-fast".
L264: 
L265:     from tabpfn.constants import ModelVersion
L266: 
L267:     classifier = TabPFNClassifier.create_default_for_version(ModelVersion.V3_5_FAST)
L268:     regressor = TabPFNRegressor.create_default_for_version(ModelVersion.V3_5_FAST)
L269: To use other model versions (e.g. the previous default, TabPFN-3):
L270: 
L271:     classifier = TabPFNClassifier.create_default_for_version(ModelVersion.V3)
L272:     regressor = TabPFNRegressor.create_default_for_version(ModelVersion.V3)
